question_text: A store marks up an item by 25% from its cost of P2,400. What is the marked price?

hint_ladder.title: Kilalanin ang Markup
hint_ladder.text: Markup means magdadagdag ka ng porsyento sa original cost. Dito, 25% ang idadagdag sa P2,400. Compute muna ang 25% ng P2,400.

hint_ladder.title: Percent to Decimal
hint_ladder.text: 25% = 0.25 or 1/4. I-multiply sa cost: 0.25 × 2,400. Ito ang dagdag na halaga. Mag-ingat sa multiplication.

hint_ladder.title: Kuwentahin ang Markup Amount
hint_ladder.text: 0.25 × 2,400 = 600. Iyan ang profit. Ngayon, idagdag sa original cost para makuha ang marked price. So 2,400 + 600.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you thought 25% of 2,400 is 400 (maybe using 1,600). The real markup is 600, leading to 3,000.

B.text: You might have chosen B because you got 500 as markup (using 20% or a slip). The correct amount is 600, so the marked price is 3,000.

C.text: Correct. 25% of P2,400 is P600, so marked price = P2,400 + P600 = P3,000.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you added 800 (maybe used 33% instead of 25%). The right markup is 600, so the price is 3,000.

next_time_rule: Marked Price = Cost × (1 + markup rate). For 25% markup: multiply cost by 1.25. Alalahanin: 1 + rate na decimal.
deconstruct_text:
Imagine si Aling Nena may sari-sari store. Bumili siya ng item sa P2,400. Para kumita, nag-mark up siya ng 25%.

Una, kunin ang 25% ng original cost. 25% ay same as 0.25 or 1/4. So 0.25 × 2,400 = 600. Yan ang dagdag.

Ngayon, i-add ang dagdag sa original: 2,400 + 600 = 3,000. Yan na ang marked price.

Puwede ring shortcut: 2,400 × 1.25 (since 100% + 25% = 125%) = 3,000. Tama din.

Common na pagkakamali dito ay mali ang kuwenta ng 25% of 2,400, like 400 o 500. Basta tandaan, 25% ay isang quarter, at ang quarter ng 2,400 ay 600. Kaya laging double-check ang multiplication.
